chunks: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Qattan narrated to us, saying: Abu Bakr Abdullah ibn Suleiman ibn al-Ash'ath narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Yusuf ibn Salim al-Salami narrated to us, saying: Umar ibn Abdullah ibn Razin narrated to us, saying: Sufyan ibn al-Husayn narrated from Sa'id ibn Amr ibn Ashwa', from al-Sha'bi, from Jabir ibn Samurah, saying:

I was with my father in the mosque while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was delivering a sermon. I heard him say: 'Twelve Caliphs.' Then he lowered his voice so I did not know what he was saying. I asked my father, 'What did he say?' He said, 'He said: They are all from Quraysh.'
ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the number and tribe of the Caliphs after him?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *al-Khisal*, this hadith establishes the foundational Shia belief in the twelve divinely appointed successors, emphasizing their Qurayshi lineage as a criterion for legitimacy. The narration's inclusion of the Prophet's whispering of the phrase 'all of them from Quraysh' underscores the continuity of authority within the Prophet's own tribe, a key point of distinction in Shia political theology. This tradition serves as a primary textual evidence for the number and tribal origin of the Imams, linking prophetic prediction directly to the lineage of Ali and the Twelve Imams.
